title: Applying and reversing a BPE tokenizer
description: A quick reference for the frozen-tokenizer, control-token, and exact-decoding terms used here.

terms.definition: A tokenizer that starts with all byte values and applies learned merges to frequent byte sequences.
A learned rule whose fixed rank determines application priority without recounting pairs on new input.
The single token segmentation produced by replaying frozen merge ranks in their defined order.
A non-control token representing one byte or a learned byte sequence in document content.
A structural token marking a document boundary instead of representing content bytes.
Beginning-of-sequence and end-of-sequence controls placed only at document endpoints after content encoding.
The shift applied to content-token IDs so the first two IDs remain reserved for controls.
A one-byte content token used when no learned merge covers that byte.
Recovering token byte expansions in order so the output bytes exactly match the original input.
An optional text conversion that reports invalid UTF-8 instead of altering or replacing recovered bytes.
